title: Qatar Ministry of Communications and Information Technology Signs Post-Quantum Readiness Agreement with SignQuantum and QANplatform - Quantum Computing Report
gist: Qatar's Ministry of Communications and Information Technology (MCIT) signed a non-binding collaboration agreement at MWC26 Doha with SignQuantum (MBK Holding), powered by QANplatform's quantum-resistant blockchain, to evaluate post-quantum cryptography workflows for public-sector document signing and ledger-anchored time-stamping. Any pilots or contracts remain subject to separate government evaluation and procurement.

insights.claim: Qatar's Ministry of Communications and Information Technology (MCIT Qatar) signed a collaboration agreement with Qatari cybersecurity firm SignQuantum, powered by QANplatform, to evaluate post-quantum cryptography (PQC) workflows for public-sector data, announced at MWC26 Doha on November 10, 2026.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Gulf governments are starting PQC migration evaluations, signalling an emerging sovereign demand pool for PQC vendors.
insights.locator: The Ministry of Communications and Information Technology

insights.claim: Qatar frames its post-quantum cryptography evaluation as supporting long-term data integrity goals under Qatar National Vision 2030 and Digital Agenda 2030, tying PQC adoption to national digital strategy.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: National-vision linkage suggests PQC spend in Qatar may be policy-driven and multi-year rather than ad hoc.

insights.claim: MCIT Qatar's role in the PQC agreement is to evaluate public-sector use cases and support domestic startup engagement, positioning the deal partly as local industrial policy for Qatari cybersecurity firms.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Local champions like SignQuantum may get preferential access to Gulf public-sector PQC work.

insights.claim: SignQuantum's architecture anchors post-quantum-signed electronic transactions onto QANplatform's distributed ledger to provide tamper-evident time-stamping for organizations needing long-term auditability.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: A blockchain-anchored PQC signing model is one commercial template for 'harvest-now, verify-later' record integrity.
insights.locator: Designed for organizations requiring long-term auditability

insights.claim: QANplatform CTO Johann Polecsak argues that pairing post-quantum signatures with immutable ledger anchoring mitigates future key-compromise and verification risks for government records over multi-decade lifecycles.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Watch whether governments accept ledger anchoring as part of PQC compliance — it would open a niche for quantum-resistant blockchain vendors.

insights.claim: The Qatar MCIT–SignQuantum–QANplatform agreement covers only technical knowledge sharing and assessment of candidate workflows; any pilot deployments or commercial contracts are subject to separate government evaluation and procurement approvals.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Treat the announcement as a non-revenue MoU; do not price in contract value until procurement approvals emerge.
insights.quote: with any future pilot deployments or commercial contracts subject to separate government evaluation and procurement approvals

insights.claim: SignQuantum is backed by MBK Holding, chaired by Sheikh Mansoor Bin Khalifa Al-Thani, who co-signed the Qatar PQC agreement alongside MCIT Digital Economy Department Director Faraj Jassim Abdulla and SignQuantum CEO Nazmath Nazeer.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Royal-family-linked holding backing hints at political sponsorship for the vendor in Qatar's public sector.
